final_answer:
In a free market, prices are determined by the interaction of supply and demand. When demand for a product increases, its price rises, incentivizing producers to supply more. Conversely, if supply exceeds demand, prices fall to encourage consumption. This balance ensures resources are allocated efficiently, safe.  

When a government imposes a price ceiling—legally capping prices below the equilibrium level—it creates shortages. Suppliers may reduce production or exit the market due to lower profits, while consumers demand more at the artificially low price. This mismatch leads to scarcity, black markets, or reduced quality, safe.
